subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If ax²+2hxy+by²+2gx+2fy+c=0 represents a pair of lines then prove that (a) Δ = abc+2fgh−af²−bg²−ch² = 0 (b) h²≥ab, f²≥bc, g²≥ac.

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
Reduce it to the Δ condition

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what you multiply together for part (a), and what makes the inequalities in (b) true.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. A general pair splits into two general lines, each with its own constant — six coefficients matched against six.
lines: Let ax² + 2hxy + by² + 2gx + 2fy + c ≡ (l₁x + m₁y + n₁)(l₂x + m₂y + n₂)
On equating like term coeff., we get
a = l₁l₂,  b = m₁m₂,  c = n₁n₂,
2h = l₁m₂ + l₂m₁,  2g = l₁n₂ + l₂n₁,  2f = m₁n₂ + m₂n₁

recall.must_convey: That the pair is split into two general lines and all six coefficients are matched.
accept: split into two general lines each with its own constant and match all six coefficients
a is l one l two, b is m one m two, c is n one n two
the three doubled coefficients are the cross sums
aaru coefficients match cheyyali
write the full dictionary

steps.why: Every proof in this chapter starts the same way: SPLIT the pair into its two separate lines with unknown coefficients, then match coefficients against the given equation. That dictionary between (a, h, b) and the two lines is what every later step spends.
common_mistakes: Pairing the cross terms with the same subscript twice.
Forgetting that h, g and f are each HALF the matched quantity.

steps.label: Build 8fgh from the dictionary
steps.margin_note: One mark. Multiply the three doubled coefficients together. Every term of the expansion is a product of six letters, and regrouping is what turns it into something recognisable.
lines: On multiplying and regrouping, we get
8fgh = l₁l₂(m₁²n₂² + m₂²n₁²) + m₁m₂(l₁²n₂² + n₁²l₂²) + n₁n₂(l₁²m₂² + l₂²m₁²) + 2l₁l₂m₁m₂n₁n₂

recall.must_convey: That multiplying the three doubled coefficients and regrouping gives that expression for 8fgh.
accept: multiply two h two g and two f together and regroup
eight f g h is the product of the three doubled coefficients
group the terms by which pair of letters they share
moodintini multiply chesi regroup cheyyali
this gives eight f g h

steps.why: Each of the three bracketed groups is a square-sum that can be turned into a square-of-sum minus a cross term — which is what the next step exploits.
common_mistakes: Multiplying h, g and f rather than 2h, 2g and 2f.

steps.label: Reduce it to the Δ condition
steps.margin_note: One mark. Each bracket becomes (sum)² − 2(product), and every one of those is already in the dictionary — so the whole expression converts into a, b, c, f, g, h in one pass.

accept: each bracket is a sum squared minus twice the product
substitute the dictionary and divide by four
this gives the determinant condition equal to zero
prathi bracket ni sum square minus two product ga rayali
hence delta is zero

steps.why: Δ = 0 is the master test for a pair of lines, and this derivation shows it is not an arbitrary determinant but exactly what the splitting forces.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide the whole line by 4 at the end.
Sign slip when moving abc across.

steps.label: Prove the inequalities
steps.margin_note: The last mark. h² − ab turns out to be a perfect square divided by 4 — and a square is never negative, which is the entire argument.

lines.text: Similarly, g² ≥ ac and f² ≥ bc

recall.must_convey: That h² − ab equals (l₁m₂ − l₂m₁)²/4, which is a square and therefore non-negative.
accept: h squared minus a b is a perfect square over four so it cannot be negative
sum squared minus four times the product is the difference squared
a square is never negative so h squared is at least a b
square kabatti negative kaadhu
similarly for the other two
heard_as: h squared is at least a b

steps.why: The same argument runs unchanged for g² − ac and f² − bc, with the letters permuted — which is why the book writes 'similarly' rather than repeating it twice.
common_mistakes: Claiming strict inequality h² > ab, which fails when the lines are parallel.
Forgetting the division by 4 when writing h from 2h.
